tagline: For a secure, affordable and sustainable energy future.
hero_kpi_rationale: Marked recovery in operating margin (+6.3 pts) reflecting the rebound in oil prices and cost reductions following a very difficult 2015.
company_description: BP p.l.c. is an international energy group engaged in the exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil, natural gas and petroleum products, as well as low-carbon energy.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: The portion of revenue that remains after paying the direct costs of production.
kpis.description: Gross margin improves slightly in 2016, driven by cost optimization in refining operations.
kpis.signal: Stability despite a volatile energy environment

kpis.name: Operating Margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit before taxes as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin increases significantly due to the recovery in oil prices and cost reductions.
kpis.signal: Strong rebound following a heavily impacted 2015

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on building or acquiring productive facilities.
kpis.description: BP maintains a disciplined capex policy to strengthen its financial resilience after a challenging period.
kpis.signal: Significant reduction in capex amid financial discipline

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.description: BP reduces its workforce to 74,500 employees to adapt to a leaner model following the oil crisis.
kpis.signal: Workforce reduction as part of a restructuring

kpis.name: R&D Investment (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Portion of revenue dedicated to research and development.
kpis.description: BP allocates a marginal share of its revenue to R&D, typical for an integrated energy company.
kpis.signal: Very low R&D compared to tech standards, normal for an energy company

kpis.name: Hydrocarbon Production
kpis.explanation: Total volume of crude oil and natural gas produced per day.
kpis.description: BP produced 3.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day in 2016, up 3% from 2015, driven by the start-up of new projects.
kpis.signal: Slight increase in production despite low price environment

kpis.name: Proved Reserves Replacement Ratio
kpis.explanation: Ratio of reserves discovered to reserves produced during the year, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: BP replaced 109% of its proved reserves production in 2016, including the impact of the renewal of the onshore Abu Dhabi oil concession.
kpis.signal: Excellent reserves replacement ratio above 100%, including renewal of key concessions

kpis.name: Underlying RC Profit
kpis.explanation: Measures BP's underlying profit by excluding accounting fluctuations, showing actual operational performance.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Measures BP's net debt after cash deduction. Indicates financial health and repayment capacity.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Measures BP's underlying profit by excluding exceptional items to show stable operational performance.

kpis.name: Dividend per Ordinary Share
kpis.explanation: Measures the amount in euros paid annually to each shareholder: higher means higher returns.

kpis.name: Refining Availability
kpis.explanation: Measures the percentage of time BP's refineries operate at full capacity, a key profitability indicator.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 12.3868 GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 5.059 Bn GBp in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last three fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 9198.2% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Earnings per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Persistent provisions related to the Gulf of America oil spill
risks.summary: BP still carries nearly 7 billion USD in provisions and liabilities related to the Gulf of America oil spill (Deepwater Horizon). Cash outflows remain active (396 M$ in Q1 2026) and final amounts remain uncertain, exposing the group to potential provision overruns.
risks.score_rationale: Provisions and liabilities related to the Gulf of America spill amounted to 6.938 billion USD as of March 31, 2026, with explicit uncertainty over the final amount and payment timing. The language used ('amounts ultimately payable may differ', 'timing of payments is uncertain') indicates significant and uncapped residual exposure.

risks.title: Sector-specific tax pressure from the UK Energy Profits Levy
risks.summary: The UK's Energy Profits Levy (EPL) imposes an effective tax rate of 78% on BP's North Sea operations, extended to 2030. This sector-specific surcharge structurally reduces the profitability of UK upstream assets and triggers recurring revaluations of deferred tax assets.
risks.score_rationale: The Energy Profits Levy (EPL) raises the effective tax rate on North Sea profits to 78%, an exceptionally high level. The extension of the EPL to March 31, 2030 was substantially adopted in Q1 2025, with material impacts on deferred tax assets reviewed in Q1 2026, signaling a sustained adverse regulatory trend.

risks.title: Volatility in hydrocarbon realizations and exposure to market prices
risks.summary: BP's revenues are directly exposed to fluctuations in oil (Brent, WTI) and natural gas (Henry Hub, NBP) prices. European gas realizations halved in one year, illustrating the sensitivity of operating profit to energy commodity price cycles.
risks.score_rationale: Average realizations on liquids range from 51.20 $/bbl (US) to 85.35 $/bbl (Europe) in Q1 2026, with significant quarter-on-quarter variations (e.g., European natural gas: 8.76 $/mcf in Q1 2026 vs 16.47 $/mcf in Q1 2025). This dispersion illustrates a structural dependence on commodity spot prices, central to BP's business model.

risks.title: Rising environmental costs and provisions
risks.summary: BP's operational environmental costs surged to 2.4 billion USD in Q1 2026, reflecting growing obligations related to emissions, site remediation and sector-specific environmental regulations. This upward trend pressures margins in upstream and refining segments.
risks.score_rationale: Variable environmental costs reached 2.399 billion USD in Q1 2026, up 79% from Q1 2025 (1.337 Bn$). Environmental provisions are a recurring adjustment item (173 M$ in Q1 2026), signaling intensifying regulatory obligations and operational environmental liabilities.

risks.title: Ongoing restructuring and operational rationalization
risks.summary: BP is executing a significant restructuring program generating quarterly charges of around 250-350 M$. This process exposes the group to execution risks (loss of expertise, operational disruption, delays) amid a strategic transformation toward low-carbon energy.
risks.score_rationale: Restructuring, integration and rationalization costs amounted to 249 M$ in Q1 2026 and 344 M$ in Q1 2025, absent in Q4 2025, indicating an active but irregular transformation program. These recurring charges signal execution risks in portfolio and workforce reorganization.

risks.title: Accounting complexity of physical commodity contracts treated as derivatives
risks.summary: IFRS standards require BP to account for certain physical crude, LNG and transportation capacity contracts as fair value derivatives, creating recurring distortions between actual economic performance and reported results, complicating sector analysis.
risks.score_rationale: BP details the fair value accounting effects from treating physical contracts (LNG, pipelines, storage) as derivatives under IFRS, generating recurring and significant valuation gaps between actual economic performance and reported IFRS results. This representation risk affects result transparency for investors.

risks.title: High debt and pressure on deleveraging in a low-price environment
risks.summary: BP's net debt (excluding leases) increased by 3.1 billion USD in one quarter to reach 25.3 billion USD, reflecting significant working capital needs and outflows related to the Gulf of America. In a moderate oil price environment, the deleveraging trajectory and maintenance of shareholder distributions are under pressure.
risks.score_rationale: Net debt reached 25.3 Bn$ (38.6 Bn$ including leases) in Q1 2026, with a gearing ratio of 33.4% including leases. Net debt increased by 3.1 Bn$ in one quarter, amid declining Brent prices to 81 $/bbl, signaling tension on deleveraging capacity and the share buyback program.

risks.title: Energy transition and low-carbon portfolio repositioning
risks.summary: BP is transitioning its portfolio toward low-carbon energy (solar, offshore wind, hydrogen, CCS) while divesting certain renewable assets (onshore wind by end-2025). The reputational risk is twofold: being seen as insufficiently committed to transition by ESG investors, or as sacrificing short-term profitability by traditional shareholders.
risks.score_rationale: The divestment of onshore wind activities (December 2025) and continued focus on solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and CCS illustrate an ongoing strategic repositioning. The lack of demonstrated profitability in these segments creates reputational and execution risks relative to BP's public climate commitments.

ai_positioning.summary: BP does not mention any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in the 20-F 2016 document. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No mention of AI, machine learning or advanced algorithms in the report
No reference to tech AI partnerships or acquisitions
Absence of KPIs or projects related to intelligent automation
